- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend (e.g., if sentiment turns bearish, forecast should slope down).
